en.title: Microsoft Apologizes for Global Outage and Reports Restoration Progress
en.dek: Microsoft issued an apology and reported progress in restoring Outlook, Teams, and Copilot services following a technical failure that caused disruptions lasting over 18 hours.
facts: Microsoft issued an apology on Friday for a technical failure that disrupted Outlook email services worldwide.
The outage left millions of Outlook users without access to mailboxes for more than 18 hours starting on Thursday.
The company ruled out a cyberattack as the cause of the disruptions to Outlook, Teams, and Copilot.
European lawmakers called for measures to reduce reliance on foreign technology companies following the event.
Affected customers can request service credits for the interruption.
body: Microsoft issued an apology on Friday, 13 November 2026, after a global technical failure disrupted its Outlook email services for more than 18 hours. The company stated that affected customers can request service credits for the interruption, according to Variety.

Engineers made progress on Friday in restoring access to email, messaging, and assistant applications following a second day of disruptions, according to reporting by the New York Times and Semafor. Microsoft ruled out a cyberattack as the cause of the issues affecting Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, as reported by the New York Times and El País.

Access to mailboxes stopped for millions of Outlook users starting on Thursday, 12 November 2026. Services began returning to normal after more than 18 hours of continuous disruption, according to El País.

Lawmakers across Europe called for policy changes to lessen reliance on a small group of foreign technology firms after the system failure occurred, according to Politico Europe. The incident led to renewed requests from European officials to reduce dependence on software providers based in the United States.
en.context: The disruptions impacted Microsoft online services worldwide beginning on Thursday, 12 November 2026, before recovery efforts began on Friday.
